eyebrow: SQL Dialects: T-SQL, PL/SQL, MySQL & Beyond · Chapter Six
subtitle: Lesson 35 · PL/SQL Deep Dive for T-SQL Developers

caption: Every PL/SQL program is built from this same DECLARE / BEGIN / EXCEPTION / END shape.
DECLARE and EXCEPTION are both optional; BEGIN...END never is.

eyebrow: Blocks nest, each with its own scope
caption: A nested block's DECLARE section is scoped only to that inner block.

eyebrow: T-SQL's BEGIN...END has no equivalent scope
code:
-- T-SQL: BEGIN...END only groups statements
-- DECLARE @x INT inside it is still batch-scoped,
-- not scoped to that BEGIN...END
IF 1 = 1
BEGIN
  DECLARE @x INT = 5;
END;
caption: No unifying block concept in T-SQL — just statement grouping, no own scope or exception section.

eyebrow: A named procedure is this same block, named
code:
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE show_count (p_dept_id IN NUMBER) IS
  v_count NUMBER;  -- IS = DECLARE, renamed
BEGIN
  SELECT COUNT(*) INTO v_count
  FROM employees WHERE department_id = p_dept_id;
END show_count;
/
caption: Procedures, functions, triggers, and packages are all this block with a name attached.
